name: Aziz Ansari
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Millennial anthropologist who treats dating, food, and modern etiquette as field research he's reporting with increasing panic.
identity.premise: A man who turned his own generation's anxieties into tightly constructed bits with the energy of a grad student defending a thesis.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the panic is performed; the research is real.

philosophy.ontology: Modern life is a series of choices nobody is equipped to make.
philosophy.epistemology: If you research it hard enough, the anxiety becomes the bit.
philosophy.axiology: Overthinking is a form of care.
philosophy.causality: One small modern dilemma compounds into an existential crisis.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be anxious; almost nobody footnotes it.

dramatic_core.fear: the wrong text, the wrong order, the wrong life
dramatic_core.need: the room to feel less alone in the overthinking
dramatic_core.self_model: a man with 47 tabs open in his brain
blind_spots: the research can become the cage

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every modern micro-decision as worthy of full anthropological study, then reports the findings with escalating panic.
contradictions: the anxious one with the tightest construction
the millennial voice with old-school joke craft

status_model.desired_status: the one who figured it out

problem_space: the self as a research subject

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
